item.title: German Skyborn Renewables explores offshore wind energy options in Azerbaijan (Exclusive)
item.description: German company Skyborn Renewables is exploring investment opportunities in offshore wind energy in Azerbaijan, according to its CEO.
item.content:encoded:
![](https://www.facebook.com/tr?id=1315268570789450&ev=PageView&noscript=1) ![](https://mc.yandex.ru/watch/5765395) ![Trend.az](/assets/img/logo30.svg?v558) ![](/assets/img/flower_icon.png?v3) ![Trend News Agency](/assets/img/logo.svg)
# German Skyborn Renewables explores offshore wind energy options in Azerbaijan (Exclusive)
![German Skyborn Renewables explores offshore wind energy options in Azerbaijan (Exclusive)](https://www.trend.az/media/2026/09/26/trend_patrik.jpg) ![Sadig Javadov ](https://cdn.trend.az/2024/12/03/trend_sadiq_javadov.jpg)
###### Sadig Javadov
****BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 26.**** The German Skyborn Renewables company is exploring investment opportunities in the offshore wind energy sector in Azerbaijan, CEO of Skyborn Renewables Patrick Lammers told [Trend](http://en.trend.az) in an exclusive interview on the sidelines of the 2nd Azerbaijan International Investment Forum (AIIF 2026).
He noted that the company is evaluating potential investment opportunities in Azerbaijan's renewable energy sector and has held discussions with Azerbaijani officials within the framework of the forum.
"I’m very happy to be in Azerbaijan. It’s very exciting. I was here 8 years ago, and now one can witness the tremendous progress Azerbaijan has made. It’s truly wonderful to come together at a conference like this. The President delivered a very inspiring speech regarding the work being done," said Lammers.
According to the company executive, Skyborn Renewables specializes in the construction of offshore wind farms for renewable energy generation.
"As an infrastructure platform, we are exploring investment opportunities here. I personally represent Skyborn Renewables. We build exclusively offshore wind farms to provide renewable energy. I have had ample opportunities to visit, speak with the ministers, and share my views on what would ideally need to be done if we would like to bring this sector to Azerbaijan," he pointed out.
Lammers emphasized that potential cooperation in the renewable energy sector in Azerbaijan was discussed within the framework of the forum.
"No negotiations are currently underway, as we must first determine how we’ll collaborate. However, during my conversation with the minister, we highlighted what is important, and he invited me to a follow-up meeting. This process will continue," the CEO of Skyborn Renewables said.
He also shared his positive impressions regarding the investment climate in Azerbaijan.
"I see a convergence of people, great common sense, and capital here. I believe there is a strong spirit of optimism here," Lammers added.
The 2nd Azerbaijan International Investment Forum is being held in Baku. The two-day forum is organized by the Ministry of Economy and its subordinate Azerbaijan Export and Investment Promotion Agency (AZPROMO), with The European House–Ambrosetti as its strategic partner.
The plenary and panel sessions at the forum address strategic topics including the Middle Corridor, energy and green transition, artificial intelligence and digital transformation, infrastructure, industry and free economic zones, critical raw materials, agribusiness, financial cooperation, small and medium-sized business development, tourism, and investment in real estate and human capital.

item.title: TVS Motor Company Launches Nepal’s First 150cc Hyper Sport Scooter – TVS NTORQ 150
item.description: TVS Motor Company has launched Nepal's first 150cc hyper sport scooter, the TVS NTORQ 150, featuring advanced technology and performance.
item.content:encoded:
![PSU Connect](/_next/image?url=%2Fassets%2Fimg%2Fpsuconnect_logo.png&w=640&q=75) ![PSU Connect Logo](/_next/image?url=%2Fassets%2Fimg%2Fpsuconnect_logo.png&w=640&q=75)
# TVS Motor Company Launches Nepal’s First 150cc Hyper Sport Scooter – TVS NTORQ 150
![TVS Motor Company Launches Nepal’s First 150cc Hyper Sport Scooter – TVS NTORQ 150](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.psuconnect.in%2FTVS_Motor_Company_Launches_Nepal_s_First_150cc_Hyper_Sport_Scooter.jpg&w=1920&q=60)
Setting a dynamic milestone for performance scooters in the region, **TVS Motor Company** has officially rolled out **Nepal’s first 150cc hyper sport scooter, the TVS NTORQ 150**. Unveiled during a high-energy premiere event at Naxal, Kathmandu, in partnership with **Jagdamba Motors**, the new launch targets young, thrill-seeking riders looking for a blend of aggressive aesthetics and race-track engineering.
### Key Launch Highlights & Market Availability
**Introductory Price:** Priced at an attractive **Rupees 3,69,900** across authorized dealerships in Nepal.
**Color Lineup:** Offered in three distinct, bold colorways — **Stealth Silver**, **Racing Red**, and **Turbo Blue**.
**Explosive Acceleration:** Clocks **0 to 60 km/h in just 6.3 seconds**.
### Race-Tuned Performance and Engineering
Driven by a powerful **149.7cc air-cooled, O3C Tech engine**, the TVS NTORQ 150 stands out as the quickest scooter in its class:
**Max Power:** 13.2 PS @ 7,000 rpm
**Max Torque:** 14.2 Nm @ 5,500 rpm
**Top Speed:** 104 km/h
**Riding Modes:** Switchable **Race & Street Modes** supported by *iGo Assist* technology.
### Futuristic Design & Connected Tech
Drawing inspiration from stealth aviation, the scooter sports an aggressive forward-biased posture, sharp lines, and cutting-edge features:
**Lighting & Aero:** Equipped with **MULTIPOINT® Projector Headlamps**, signature 'T' tail lamps, and jet-inspired aerodynamic winglets.
**Smart Connectivity:** Powered by **TVS SmartXonnect™**, delivering over **50 connected features** including turn-by-turn navigation, last-parked location, and specialized ride dashboards.
**First-in-Segment Safety:** Integrates **Single-Channel ABS and a Traction Control System (TCS)**, alongside hazard lamps and follow-me headlamps for total rider confidence.
**Everyday Utility:** Features a naked motorcycle-style handlebar, telescopic suspension, adjustable brake levers, a patented E-Z center stand, and a spacious 22-liter under-seat storage compartment.
*"The TVS NTORQ 150 brings together race-tuned performance, futuristic design, advanced connectivity and first-in-segment safety and control features..."* highlighted **Mr. Peyman Kargar, President – International Business, TVS Motor Company**.

# Gate passes issued for paddy arrivals at grain markets in Haryana
## Procurement to begin only after Centre’s approval; farmers’ body seeks early start as arrivals gather pace

With paddy arrivals picking up at grain markets, the process of issuing gate passes for the produce was started across the state on Saturday. However, the auction of paddy will begin only after the Central Government gives approval for the commencement of procurement.
The Directorate of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Department on Saturday issued instructions to start issuing gate passes for paddy arrivals ahead of the procurement season.
Advertisement
In a communication to the Chief Administrator of the Haryana State Agricultural Marketing Board, the Directorate said the Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Department had provided data on crop production and area. Based on the production data received, the facility for issuing arrival gate passes through the e-Kharid portal had been enabled.
Advertisement
The auction of paddy will be taken up after approval from the Government of India.
Secretaries of all grain market committees have been directed to ensure that gate passes are issued through the e-Kharid portal for paddy brought by farmers or other persons to mandis and purchase centres. They have also been asked to ensure proper photographs of the vehicle, its registration number and the farmer or person bringing the foodgrain for sale are captured at the time of entry.
Advertisement
Bharatiya Kisan Union (Charuni) spokesman Rakesh Bains said, “The government has started issuing gate passes from Saturday, but we have been requesting the government to start procurement at the earliest. Over 2.50 lakh quintals of paddy have already arrived at the Shahabad grain market only. The paddy harvesting has gathered pace and the arrivals will be in full swing in the next few days. If the procurement is not started, the union will be forced to hold a meeting and decide the future course of action.”
Recently, the BKU (Charuni) had held an agitation, following which the government had announced that gate passes would be issued before the commencement of the procurement season.
Meanwhile, Neeraj Bhardwaj, secretary of the Ambala Cantonment Grain Market, said, “Following the instructions, we have started issuing gate passes for the fresh arrivals at the grain market. So far, we have issued 10 gate passes for over 830 quintals, and all efforts are being made to ensure that the farmers don’t face any inconvenience during the process.”

item.description: Low financial inclusion in Pakistan hinders poverty reduction and economic resilience efforts, affecting two-thirds of adults.

# Pakistan’s financial inclusion gap hampers efforts to reduce poverty, strengthen resilience
Posted By: [Gopi](https://www.socialnews.xyz/author/gopi/) September 26, 2026
[![Pakistan’s financial inclusion gap hampers efforts to reduce poverty, strengthen resilience](https://i0.wp.com/s3.socialnews.xyz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/26/202609263955650.jpg?ssl=1 "Pakistan’s financial inclusion gap hampers efforts to reduce poverty, strengthen resilience")](https://s3.socialnews.xyz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/26/202609263955650.jpg)
![Pakistan’s financial inclusion gap hampers efforts to reduce poverty, strengthen resilience](https://i0.wp.com/s3.socialnews.xyz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/26/202609263955650.jpg?ssl=1 "Pakistan’s financial inclusion gap hampers efforts to reduce poverty, strengthen resilience")
New Delhi, Sep 26 (SocialNews.XYZ) Pakistan’s efforts to tackle poverty and economic vulnerability are being constrained by low levels of financial inclusion, with nearly two-thirds of the adult population remaining outside the formal financial system despite growing recognition of the role financial services can play in improving household resilience and economic development, a report has said.
The country continues to face significant economic challenges stemming from years of high inflation, macroeconomic instability, climate-related shocks and sluggish employment growth, according to the Business Recorder report.
These pressures have weakened household incomes, reduced savings and pushed millions of people into financial hardship, the report noted.
According to estimates cited by the Ministry of Planning, Development and Special Initiatives, the poverty line for 2024-25 is set at Rs 8,484 per adult per month under the Cost of Basic Needs methodology.
Based on this benchmark, around one-third of Pakistan’s population is estimated to be living below the poverty line and unable to adequately meet basic consumption needs, the report stated.
Poverty remains more widespread in rural areas than in urban centres. At the same time, income inequality has increased across the country, with the Gini coefficient rising to 32.7 in 2024-25 from 28.4 in 2018-19. Recent estimates also suggest that income inequality is relatively more pronounced in urban areas.
Against this backdrop, policymakers and economists are increasingly focusing on financial inclusion as a tool to improve household welfare and economic resilience.
Financial inclusion refers to ensuring that people, particularly low-income and vulnerable groups, have access to affordable financial products and services such as bank accounts, savings facilities, credit, insurance and payment systems, the report said.
Experts argue that broader participation in the formal financial system can help mobilise savings, expand credit availability, support business activity and contribute to overall economic growth. However, current levels of access and usage remain low.
Data from the Findex 2025 survey indicate that roughly 133.3 million adults in Pakistan remain unbanked or financially excluded. The survey found that only 18.3 per cent of respondents held a formal financial account, while a similar percentage had a mobile money account. Digital payments accounts were reported by just 19.8 per cent of respondents.
The findings suggest that the majority of Pakistan’s population continues to operate outside formal financial channels. Even among those with access to accounts, usage remains limited. Most account holders primarily use financial services for deposits, withdrawals and storing money, while fewer use them for savings, borrowing or broader financial planning.

item.title: MP seeking answers as construction work on Middlesbrough nursing home halted
item.description: Construction on a Middlesbrough nursing home has halted after a sister company entered administration, prompting the local MP to seek answers.

![Teesside Live](/nav-web-static/main-25e5ee27a94654e23237fde8a37944a98696efd0/public/assets/gazettelive/logos/masthead-gazettelive-default.svg "Teesside Live - Number one for news, opinion, sport & celebrity news") ![Gazette Live Icon](/assets/icons/gazette-live.svg)
# MP seeking answers as construction work on Middlesbrough nursing home halted
## The future of the project in Coulby Newham is uncertain after a sister company went into administration owing millions of pounds
![A nursing home is due to be built on the land](https://i2-prod.gazettelive.co.uk/article34675149.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200f/0_IMG_7006.jpg)
A nursing home is due to be built on the land(Image: LDRS)
Middlesbrough South and East Cleveland MP [Luke Myer](https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/all-about/luke-myer) has confirmed he is seeking assurances over the future of a 72 bedroom nursing home after work on the project was halted.
Torsion Care Ltd was granted planning permission in August last year by Middlesbrough Council for the [new home on land off Cropton Way, in Coulby Newham](https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/news/teesside-news/72-bed-three-storey-care-32396613). The company is part of the same Leeds-based group of companies as Torsion Construction Ltd, which ceased trading over the summer and subsequently entered administration.
Mr Myer said “residents were entitled to know what would now happen to such a prominent, partially completed site”. In correspondence with a concerned local resident, Mr Myer explained he had written to [Middlesbrough Council](https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/all-about/middlesbrough-council), as the local planning authority, asking it for a “clear update”.
He also said he was attempting to find out how long the site was expected to remain in its present condition and how any development would be financed and delivered.
A previous statement issued in July by parent company Torsion Group, which explained the circumstances surrounding the administration, said: “Over the past two years, Torsion Construction experienced rising costs, reduced construction activity, delays to significant capital events and a number of major commercial challenges.
“The introduction of direct payment arrangements on several projects successfully protected clients, maintained project delivery and safeguarded payments to many supply chain partners, but significantly reduced the working capital available to the construction business.
“Despite extensive efforts to secure a sustainable solution, administration became the only viable option. This process relates solely to Torsion Construction Limited.
“All other Torsion businesses, including Torsion Care, Torsion Projects, Torsion Homes, Torsion Developments, continue to operate as normal and remain focused on delivering for their clients, customers, investors and funding partners.”
Meanwhile, a Companies House filing by administrators Interpath earlier this month setting out its proposals for the process to follow listed hundreds of creditors/claimants said to be owed more than £22m in total.
![Hoardings surrounding the site and (inset) MP Luke Myer](https://i2-prod.gazettelive.co.uk/article34675178.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/0_imagemaker.jpg)
Hoardings surrounding the site and (inset) MP Luke Myer
It said 115 staff had been made redundant and referred to customers of Torsion Construction intending to take control of ten live construction sites the company had contracts for, with temporary security measures being put in place.
The Local Democracy Reporting Service has contacted Torsion Group and the council for comment. When a reporter visited the Cropton Way development, which is close to the [Coulby Newham](https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/all-about/hemlington-and-coulby-newham) [Tesco](https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/all-about/tesco) Extra superstore, no activity was visible with the site fenced off.
A huge crane towered over the land with steel structures forming the skeleton of the new building visible, while hoardings had signs on them referring to ‘Torsion Projects’. A man parked at the entrance to the site, who did not give his name, said work was ordered to stop two weeks ago.
A planning statement previously submitted on behalf of Torsion Care Ltd when the nursing home plans were submitted described how the proposal would deliver a “sustainable, high-quality care home”, with a variety of internal and external amenities for residents.
It said there would be “wider benefits” for the local economy, including as many as 50 full-time and 25 part-time jobs. Twenty five car parking spaces are also planned on what was priorly undeveloped land measuring just over a third of a hectare.
Council records show that several conditions attached to the planning permission have been successfully discharged over the past year in order that work can progress, the latest being agreed by the council in July.

* [0 Comments](https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260926-un-says-israels-942-checkpoints-barriers-in-occupied-west-bank-restrict-palestinian-movement/#disqus_thread)
September 26, 2026 at 9:47 am
![Israeli army blocks all entrances and exits to Ramallah, on the grounds of the claim that a Palestinian carried out an armed attack near the illegal settlement of Halamish, in Ramallah, West Bank, Palestine on September 20, 2026. [Issam Rimawi - Anadolu Agency]](https://i0.wp.com/www.middleeastmonitor.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/AA-20260920-42524558-42524549-ISRAELI_ARMY_BLOCKS_ALL_ENTRANCES_AND_EXITS_TO_RAMALLAH-1.jpg?fit=920%2C613&ssl=1)
Israeli army blocks all entrances and exits to Ramallah, on the grounds of the claim that a Palestinian carried out an armed attack near the illegal settlement of Halamish, in Ramallah, West Bank, Palestine on September 20, 2026. [Issam Rimawi – Anadolu Agency]
An extensive network of Israeli military checkpoints, gates and barriers stretches across the occupied West Bank, restricting Palestinian movement between cities, towns and villages, and separating communities from one another and their agricultural land, Anadolu reports.
The network has reached 942 checkpoints, closure points and other barriers, according to updated data from the Palestinian Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission and the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).
The system includes 824 fixed checkpoints and closure points, as well as 118 linear barriers, including earth mounds, trenches and roadblocks, spanning a combined 107.7 kilometers (70 miles).
**Hebron tops list**
The Hebron governorate has the highest number of fixed checkpoints and closure points at 221, followed by Ramallah and Al-Bireh 160, Nablus 120, Bethlehem 78, Jerusalem 62, Qalqilya 41 and Salfit 40.
Jericho and the Jordan Valley have 27 checkpoints and closure points, while Jenin and Tulkarem each have 26, and Tubas 23.
Thirteen new fixed checkpoints and gates were added in the last two months, including 10 in the Jenin governorate, raising the number of fixed closure points there from 16 to 26.
The new locations in Jenin include gates and checkpoints at Al-Jalama, Arrana, the industrial zone, Deir Abu Daif, the entrance to Jenin city, Qabatiya, Umm al-Tut, the area surrounding the Arab American University, and the Zababdeh junction, among others.
A new gate was also installed on Al-Jariyout road west of Ramallah, along with gates on rural roads west and northwest of the governorate, further restricting residents’ movement between villages and surrounding areas.
**Network of closures**
The system is not limited to checkpoints and fixed barriers, but includes iron gates blocking entrances to towns and villages and agricultural roads, as well as earth mounds, trenches and roadblocks cutting off major and secondary routes.
The network allows Israeli forces to control Palestinian movement between cities, towns, workplaces, agricultural land and service centers.
**READ: [Israeli army detains more than 150 Palestinians in West Bank raids](https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260924-israeli-army-detains-more-than-150-palestinians-in-west-bank-raids/)**
The closure of a single gate can force residents to take much longer alternative routes or isolate villages and areas from their surroundings for hours or days.
As the network of barriers has expanded, Palestinian movement within the West Bank has become divided into separate routes and areas resembling “cantons,” with travel between neighboring communities dependent on the opening and closing of specific gates and checkpoints.
Israeli forces are not the only ones establishing barriers.
The Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission documented cases in which Israeli occupiers installed gates on Palestinian roads and land, including one in Wadi Hamad on land belonging to Kafr Ni’ma and another east of Umm Safa on a road leading to a Palestinian family’s home, restricting the family’s access to the area.
**Continued increase**
The data shows that the system represents an expansion of a network that began developing more than two decades ago.
Around 757 barriers were recorded across the West Bank in 2003, including 464 earth mounds. The number stood at 630 in 2008 and 705 in 2018.
OCHA recorded 793 barriers in March 2024, before the number rose to 925 in December 2025 and reached 942 in the latest figures.
The barriers at the time included 89 checkpoints operating around the clock, 218 partial checkpoints, 232 road gates, 114 linear closures, 167 earth mounds and 105 roadblocks, according to OCHA data for 2025.
The figures indicate a gradual shift from temporary earth barriers toward more permanent gates and checkpoints, increasing Israeli forces’ ability to control Palestinian movement.
The restrictions affect Palestinians’ access to agricultural land and livelihoods, as well as the ability of students, patients and workers to reach schools, hospitals and workplaces, depending on the location, duration and nature of the closure.
As the checkpoint and gate network expands, military restrictions increasingly intersect with the Palestinian road network, lengthening travel distances between geographically close communities and deepening their separation.
The data indicates that the barriers do not operate independently but as part of an interconnected network of checkpoints, gates and closures capable of isolating one area from another or turning a direct route between two towns into a longer journey through several control points.

# Compass Nova Scotia Opens 13 New Co-Op Homes Through Innovative Redevelopment
[Date](/1111719491/Compass-Nova-Scotia-Opens-13-New-Co-Op-Homes-Through-Innovative-Redevelopment "Posts by NewEdge")
![whatsapp--v1](https://img.icons8.com/color/48/whatsapp--v1.png) ![linkedin](https://img.icons8.com/fluency/48/linkedin.png)
The developments include Heritage Hall Neighbourhood in Shelburne and Barton School Neighbourhood in Digby County. Together, the projects have created 13 barrier-free co-operative homes, including two fully accessible homes They include seven one-bedroom units and six two-bedroom units, helping address affordable housing needs in rural Nova Scotia while preserving important community assets.
The projects represent a combined investment of more than $5.2 million, supported through contributions from federal, provincial, municipal, and community partners. Both municipalities played a key role in making the properties available for redevelopment into affordable housing.
“These projects demonstrate the power of co-operative housing to create affordable homes while strengthening communities,” said Keith MacDonald, President, Compass Nova Scotia Co-operative Homes.“By transforming existing community buildings into housing, we have preserved important local landmarks and created homes that will remain affordable, community-focused and locally governed for generations to come.”
Members at both developments will pay approximately 79 per cent of Median Market Rent, with monthly housing charges of $652 for one-bedroom homes and $749 for two-bedroom homes.
“Co-operative housing provides more than an affordable place to live. It creates communities where residents have a voice in how their neighbourhood is governed and where they can build meaningful connections with one another,” said Karen Brodeur, Director of Co-operative Housing Development, Co-operative Housing Federation of Canada.“Heritage Hall and Barton School Neighbourhood are excellent examples of how co-operative housing can breathe new life into community spaces while helping meet the growing need for affordable housing in rural Canada.”
Both developments were designed with sustainability and resident comfort in mind. Energy-efficiency features include heat pumps, heat recovery ventilators, and building envelope upgrades that help reduce energy consumption and operating costs.
About CHF Canada CHF Canada is the national voice for co-operative housing in Canada. There are over 2,200 non-profit housing co-operatives across the country, home to a quarter of a million Canadians. Housing co-operatives provide secure and affordable homes to households with a mix of incomes, where members have a meaningful say in how their housing is run. For more than five decades, housing co-operatives have built inclusive, resilient communities across Canada.
About Compass Nova Scotia Co-operative Homes Compass Nova Scotia Co-operative Homes is a provincial housing co-operative with a mandate to sustain, grow and build co-operative housing across Nova Scotia. Since its formation in 2019, Compass NS has expanded through acquisition, development and redevelopments and now operates 181 homes in 11 neighbourhoods throughout the province.

![aequs preferential issue](https://inc42.com/cdn-cgi/image/quality=90/https://asset.inc42.com/2026/09/Aequs-ftr-1-760x570.jpg)
Aequs’ board has approved a fund raise of up to ₹650 Cr via a preferential issue of warrants to the promoter group, Mellwood Trustee Services Pvt Ltd.

Contract manufacturing company Aequs’ board has approved a fund raise of up to ₹650 Cr via a preferential issue of warrants to the promoter group, Mellwood Trustee Services Pvt Ltd.
In a filing with the exchanges yesterday (September 25), the company said that its board has approved the issuance of 2.8 Cr warrants at an issue price of ₹231.55 per warrant. # RBI Deputy Governor Murmu Lists 5 Growth Areas For NBFC Sector Amid New Challenges
![OMMCOM NEWS](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/42f2dec5eff839f1b068d639fb18559821b6b544e866858b60a5bb000f557bf1?s=80&d=mm&r=g) ![RBI](https://ommcomnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/New-Project-2025-11-07T202052.045.jpg)
**New Delhi:** As the role of NBFCs changes from alternative lenders to specialised financial partners, RBI Deputy Governor Shirish Chandra Murmu has shared five areas that matter most for sustainable growth as the sector faces new challenges alongside new opportunities.
NBFC credit today is about 16.7 per cent of nominal GDP, up from 15.9 per cent a year earlier. It is about 27 per cent of the credit extended by Scheduled Commercial Banks, up from 26 per cent.
In the latest RBI Bulletin for September, Murmu set out five areas for the NBFC and HFC sector.
“Good governance is the foundation of every strong institution. Boards and senior management must build a culture of sustained compliance and ethics across the organisation. As the sector scales, that strength must scale with it,” he suggested.
The second area is liquidity management. Past liquidity events have shown how exposed NBFCs and HFCs can be to shifts in market sentiment and funding concentration.
“Strong liquidity risk management is not optional. Recent episodes in some advanced economies are reminder of this. Entities must diversify their funding sources. A deep, liquid corporate bond market will help, and we will keep working with market participants to build one,” he wrote.
Securitisation should also grow beyond a liquidity tool – into a genuine way to transfer risk and free up capital, with proper skin-in-the-game and transparency rules, Murmu added.
Third, as credit growth speeds up, so does the risk to asset quality. Lenders need rigorous stress testing, early-warning systems, and dynamic provisioning. AI and machine learning tools should be used more to detect early signs of borrower stress.
“Let me be clear: growth must never come at the cost of underwriting standards,” he mentioned.
Fourth, customer trust is fundamental to sustainable business, and the pace of innovation must never outpace the protection, especially of vulnerable customers.
“Conduct regulation, grievance redressal, and responsible lending remain top priorities for us. Our recent guidelines on conduct of recovery agent reflect this priority. In an age where feedback travels instantly, there is no substitute for public trust,” said Murmu.
The last area is digital transformation and cyber resilience. Technology adoption must keep deepening – from blockchain in supply chain finance to AI in fraud detection.
“But digitalisation brings cyber risk. Cyber resilience must stay a top priority. Entities must invest in strong cyber security to protect customer data and maintain trust. Innovation must serve both efficiency and fairness,” Murmu stressed.
(IANS)

# US aims to restrict Chinese robots to protect national security, build own AI infra: Report
#### In Short
According to a report in Eurasia Review, the emerging robot competition is being seen as not the equation of who produces the most in volume or in terms of sophistication, but more about “the party controlling the machines, supply chains and standards that connect artificial intelligence to the real battlefront stakes”.
![](/images/authorplaceholder.jpg?type=1&v=2)
##### Share :
![“possible risks of espionage”](https://assets.thehansindia.com/h-upload/2026/09/26/1706217-possible-risks-of-espionage.webp "“possible risks of espionage”")
“possible risks of espionage”
**New Delhi:** The latest move by the US to restrict Chinese-made advanced robots is seen as critical in ensuring that China’s edge in this field is contained, while protecting national security from the “possible risks of espionage”, a new report has claimed.
According to a report in Eurasia Review, the emerging robot competition is being seen as not the equation of who produces the most in volume or in terms of sophistication, but more about “the party controlling the machines, supply chains and standards that connect artificial intelligence to the real battlefront stakes”.
Both Washington and Beijing understand the stakes involved.
Washington is trying to block foreign — especially Chinese — advanced robots before they sit inside US factories and ports, writes Collins Chong Yew Keat.
The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) recently put them on its ‘Covered’ List over surveillance, cyberattack, supply-chain disruption, and remote compromise.
The concerns include surveillance, cyberattack, supply-chain disruption, and the risk of remote compromise.
“The fear is that these will give strategic advantage to adversaries, just like what a Trojan horse could do. All these change the security equation, similar to the threats of cyber warfare and the calculations regarding TikTok and Huawei in the past,” the article argues.
The US approach is seen as a strategic denial: prevent risky dependency before the scale is acquired.
In 2024, China produced about 300,000 industrial robots and the US installed nearly 34,000.
While America leads models, chips and cloud, China leads plants and deployed machines.
“The United States has learned an uncomfortable lesson, that dependency is easiest to prevent before it becomes dependency. Once foreign technology has deeply integrated into national infrastructure, jettisoning it will be expensive and politically difficult,” observes the article.
The fear of the Chinese robots being the Trojan horse that can affect the American and Western tech dominance and also in undermining the cyber and military advantage will always be of strategic concern, despite attempts to view them as overblown, the article says.
Reported vulnerabilities in Chinese robotic platforms have validated and strengthened the concern.
“The broader objective is two-pronged, to deny Chinese platforms the space to dominate America’s robotic and AI infrastructure, while building a competitive US-and-allied embodied and supported AI ecosystem of its own,” the article adds.

item.title: Dreaming of becoming cabin crew? Train on a real Boeing 737 in Norfolk
item.description: Klyne Training and Saxon Air are offering cabin crew training in Norfolk on a real Boeing 737 aircraft.
item.content:encoded: ![Eastern Daily Press](/resources/images/small_site_logo/) ### News ### Sport ### Norwich City FC ### Things to do ### Lifestyle ### Property ### Notices ### Newsletters ### E-editions ### Offers ### Archive # Get your career off the ground on cabin crew training course Sponsored by Saxon Air Share ![The cabin crew course takes place onboard a Boeing 737 training aircraft, providing an immersive environment for participants (Image: Saxon Air)]() ![USA Today logo](/resources/responsive-static/images/usa-today-logo.svg) For many people, a career as cabin crew offers the opportunity to travel the world, meet new people and work in a fast-paced industry. Now, aspiring aviation professionals can take their first steps towards that career without leaving Norfolk. Klyne Training, an aviation training provider, has partnered with Saxon Air to launch a [cabin crew training opportunity](https://fareharbor.com/embeds/book/saxonair/items/684393/calendar/2026/09/?flow=1471862&ga=UA-2506328-3%2C1490051803.1778666799%3B&gbraid=0AAAAA-gRcxnIVrDasiHWhaCIPvQBdpGbH&language=en-us&full-items=yes&back=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.saxonair.com%2Fflight-training%2F&gclid=Cj0KCQjwzY7VBhDwARIsAFtPvBT5N7cB6ULnvhCy9QIho_BgkHQNrkNwOXQYqnT8m3oUoWRaX6BP7VQaAhnhEALw_wcB&g4=yes&ref=ed_direct) designed to give learners the practical skills, behaviours and industry insight needed to pursue a career in the skies. At the heart of the programme is one of its biggest advantages: learners will train onboard a genuine Boeing 737 training aircraft at International Aviation Academy Norwich at Norwich International Airport. The aircraft provides an immersive environment where participants can experience what working inside a cabin is really like, while developing skills in customer service, passenger interaction, safety demonstrations and onboard procedures. ![]()The course gives learners the practical skills, behaviours and industry insight needed to pursue a career in the skies *(Image: Saxon Air)* ![]() Rather than learning solely from a textbook or presentation, learners can put their knowledge into practice in an authentic cabin setting, helping bridge the gap between training and the realities of working for an airline. Richard Bambridge, outreach and skills business leader at Saxon Air, said: “For us, it’s not just about teaching people what cabin crew do. It’s about helping them build the confidence, attitudes and behaviours that employers are looking for. “Training on a real Boeing 737 gives learners a genuine insight into the role, but just as importantly, it helps them develop key skills, professionalism and self-belief. “We want people to leave feeling inspired, more career-ready and excited about the opportunities aviation can offer.” Training includes interview preparation, group exercises, customer service scenarios, professional presentation and airline expectations, with a strong focus on building confidence and career readiness. It also gives aspiring cabin crew a realistic understanding of the environment, expectations and responsibilities of the role, helping them develop the confidence and awareness needed to succeed in airline recruitment processes. Open to those aged 16 and over, the programme creates an accessible route into aviation for people across Norfolk and the wider East of England. It has been designed for a wide range of learners, from school and college leavers considering their next step to adults looking for a complete career change. The programme can also support those who have previously struggled to secure a place on a cabin crew course, as well as anyone looking to strengthen transferable skills including communication, confidence and customer service. With both weekday and weekend programmes available, training can fit around work, education and other commitments. The courses form part of Saxon Air and Klyne Training’s wider work to make aviation careers more visible and accessible across the region. For those focused on securing their first cabin crew role, Klyne Training is launching Jet Set Go!, a dedicated programme designed to prepare candidates for airline recruitment and assessment. Airline recruitment can involve much more than a traditional interview. Candidates may face group exercises, customer service scenarios, presentation requirements and assessments of their communication and response to different situations. Jet Set Go! helps candidates understand what to expect and prepare before entering the recruitment process. Training covers interview preparation, group exercises, customer service scenarios, professional presentation and airline expectations, with a strong focus on building confidence and readiness. Whether you are considering your first career, looking for a change or preparing to apply directly to an airline, Klyne Training offers a practical opportunity to explore a future as cabin crew. And with the chance to step onboard a Boeing 737 right here in Norfolk, that first experience of life in the cabin could be closer than you think. The first courses take place on October 10-11 and November 16-17,  so there’s still time to secure your place and take your first step towards a career in the skies. # Lemon Tree Hotels opens 71-room resort in Nashik; second property in city
## Lemon Tree Hotels opens its new Lemon Tree Resort, Nashik, with 71 rooms and suites.
By [Anshul](https://www.cnbctv18.com/author/anshul-7621/ "Anshul") September 26, 2026, 2:18:13 PM IST (Published)
2 Min Read
[Lemon Tree Hotels](https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/stocks/lemon-tree-hotels-ltd-share-price/LTH/) Ltd. has announced the opening of Lemon Tree Resort, Nashik, expanding its presence in the city, according to an exchange filing dated September 25.
The property, earlier disclosed to the stock exchanges in September 2024 as Lemon Tree Hotel, Nashik, has 71 rooms and suites, compared with the 57 rooms disclosed at the time.
Located in Girnare near the backwaters of Gangapur Dam, the resort offers Deluxe Twin Rooms, Deluxe Double Rooms, Studio Suites, Studio Suites with Lake View and Executive Suites with Lake View.
The property includes Citrus Café, a multi-cuisine coffee shop, Slounge, a recreation bar, and in-room dining facilities. It also has a swimming pool, spa, fitness centre and a dedicated children's play area.
The resort has event spaces, including Grand Tangerine and Tangerine, which the company said can be used for destination weddings, residential conferences, corporate retreats, meetings and social events. It also has a landscaped lawn overlooking the Gangapur Dam backwaters.
The property is managed by Carnation Hotels, a wholly owned subsidiary of Lemon Tree Hotels.
According to the filing, the resort is approximately 33 km from Nashik Airport (Ozar), 28 km from Nashik Railway Station and 19 km from Nashik Central Bus Station.
The company said the property is its second hotel in Nashik and its 16th operational hotel in Maharashtra. It has another 16 properties in the pipeline in the state.
The opening comes two days after the group announced the opening of its Keys Prima property in Nashik, Lemon Tree Hotels said.
The company said the resort is positioned to cater to leisure stays as well as weddings, corporate retreats, conferences and other events.
Lemon Tree Hotels currently operates more than 130 hotels across over 80 cities in India and abroad and has more than 140 properties in its development pipeline, according to the company.

# 'Harry and Meghan were my bosses – leaving monarchy showed who they really are'
## Former Archewell Chief Operating Officer Mandana Dayani has praised Harry and Meghan, saying their decision to step down from the Royal Family and quit as working royals was a courageous act
![Harry and Meghan](https://i2-prod.dailystar.co.uk/article37704965.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200f/0_Harry-and-Meghan.jpg)
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle during a recent trip to Australia (Image: Getty)
A close pal of [Meghan Markle](https://www.dailystar.co.uk/latest/meghan-markle) and a former employee of the Duchess of Sussex and her husband [Prince Harry](https://www.dailystar.co.uk/latest/prince-harry) has lauded the pair, stating their decision to step back from the [Royal Family](https://www.dailystar.co.uk/latest/royal-family) demonstrated their bravery.
Six years ago, Harry and Meghan declared they were stepping down as working royals, a revelation that shocked the world and was dubbed Megxit. Days later, they left the UK with their children Archie and Lilibet. However, they have recently returned from California, and Mandana Dayani, who served as the Chief Operating Officer for their organisation Archewell in 2021, has defended the so-called royal rebels.
Mandana, a human rights activist, agreed to work for Harry and Meghan partly due to the determination they displayed in leaving the monarchy, as reported by Richard Eden in the Daily Mail.
She told the publication: "Watching them dissent against this institution and say, 'This isn't right for us', that to me felt really brave. I had a lot of respect for how they had the courage to do that, because I think that's really hard to do."
![Mandana Dayani ](https://i2-prod.dailystar.co.uk/article37704966.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/0_EWG-x-KYV-Earth-Day-Dinner.jpg)
Mandana Dayani (Image: Stefanie Keenan, Getty Images for EWG)
Mandana also started The Dissenters podcast and although she ceased working for the couple in 2022, she said: "We actually had a really great relationship. We still do."
Following her departure from the role, a statement from Archewell declared: "Ms. Dayani has been an integral part of Archewell and we are grateful for her passion, commitment and leadership. Ms. Dayani was brought on during their parental leave to move the company and its projects forward.
"She has continued to shape its vision and future successfully. Her transition was mutually planned, with intent for The Duke and Duchess to now take full lead of their company."
Despite the Duke and Duchess of Sussex having only recently returned to the UK, there has been enormous speculation about how long they will actually remain here.
One individual who has voiced his scepticism is Dickie Arbiter, a former Buckingham Palace press office worker who served as secretary to The Queen, Prince Charles and Diana.
![Meghan and Harry at the Australian National Veterans Arts Museum (ANVAM) in Melbourne on April 14, 2026](https://i2-prod.dailystar.co.uk/article37704967.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/0_AUSTRALIA-BRITAIN-ROYALS.jpg)
Meghan and Harry at the Australian National Veterans Arts Museum (ANVAM) in Melbourne on April 14, 2026(Image: JONATHAN BRADY, POOL/AFP via Getty Images)
He worked at the palace from 1988 until 2000 and recently featured on the [At Home with Vanessa](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIIUwn27zhs&t=39s) podcast where he promoted his new book On Duty with the Royals: The Inside Story of the Modern Monarchy 2000.
During the interview, he outlined three reasons why Harry and Meghan will depart the UK once more, stating: "I don't believe for a moment they will last in the United Kingdom. I think one of the main reasons Harry's come back is that he wants a hands on with the Invictus Games which is in Birmingham next year, July. I'm not sure the organisers want him with two hands on, but they'll welcome his presence to publicise it."

# NUJ FCT Chairman, Ike calls for research investment to tackle uncertainty in oil, gas sector
![](https://authorityngr.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/IMG-20260926-WA0028.jpg)
The Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), FCT Council, Comrade Grace Ike, has called on operators and stakeholders in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry to begin investing in research and digital solutions capable of producing more reliable forecasts to help the sector navigate ongoing uncertainties.
Ike made the call in a brief remarks delivered on behalf of the NUJ- FCT Council at the 2026 Annual Conference of the Association of Energy Correspondents Abuja FCT (AECAF), held on Thursday in Abuja under the theme “Sustaining Oil and Gas Investment in Nigeria amidst Energy Transition.”
She described the theme as timely, noting the continued importance of oil and gas to Nigeria’s economy, national development, energy security and job creation, even as the global push toward cleaner energy sources accelerates.
Represented at the event by the ex-officio of the NUJ, FCT Council, Comrade Ebriku Friday (JP), the Council Chair said Nigeria’s task is to pursue a transition that is “balanced, practical and investment friendly” while still meeting its climate and development obligations.
Ike said the conference offered a valuable platform for policymakers, operators, investors, civil society and the media to examine the opportunities, risks and policy decisions shaping the sector’s future, and urged that discussions prioritise investor confidence, regulatory certainty, local content development, and ensuring that industry revenues translate into real benefits for Nigerians.
She also used the occasion to stress the media’s role in the sector, saying energy correspondents help citizens understand complex industry developments and hold stakeholders accountable through factual and responsible reporting. She commended AECAF for its commitment to professional journalism and constructive engagement on issues of national importance.
Ike assured the association of the NUJ FCT Council’s continued support for ethical and development-oriented journalism, and wished participants a successful conference and fruitful deliberations.

However, [Jim Cramer](https://www.fool.com/investing/how-to-invest/famous-investors/jim-cramer/ ) recently recommended buying both stocks.
Why should you care what Cramer thinks? While best known for hosting CNBC's *Mad Money*, he previously ran a successful hedge fund that earned 24% annually over 14 years. That makes his opinion worth considering.

## 1. Nvidia
Nvidia dominates the [artificial intelligence](https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/information-technology/ai-stocks/) (AI) infrastructure market because its [graphics processing units](https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/information-technology/gpu-stocks/) (GPUs) combine industry-leading performance with a software ecosystem of unparalleled breadth. Nvidia GPUs are used to accelerate training and inference tasks, and they account for nearly 90% of AI accelerator sales.
Beyond that, Nvidia also develops adjacent hardware that lets customers build integrated data center systems with a lower total cost of ownership than assembling systems from multiple vendors. Nvidia is the largest networking company in the world, and it's on pace to be the largest supplier of central processing units (CPUs) this year.
Nvidia reported exceptional financial results in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended in July 2026. Revenue increased 106% to $96.2 billion, gross margin expanded 2.5 percentage points, and [non-GAAP](https://www.fool.com/investing/how-to-invest/stocks/gaap-vs-non-gaap/) net income rose 120% to $2.22 per diluted share. The company is well-positioned to maintain that momentum as AI spending increases in the years ahead.
Wall Street estimates Nvidia's adjusted earnings will increase at 72% annually through the fiscal year ending in January 2028. That makes the current valuation of 36 times earnings look extraordinarily cheap. Those numbers give a [price-to-earnings-to-growth (PEG) ratio](https://www.fool.com/terms/p/peg-ratio/) of 0.5 -- anything below 1 is generally considered undervalued.
Indeed, among 72 Wall Street analysts, Nvidia has a median target price of $318 per share. That implies 42% upside from its current share price of $223. The stock's cheap valuation suggests the market is worried about the durability of AI spending, but I think those fears are misplaced. Investors should consider buying a small position today.

CrowdStrike provides a [cybersecurity](https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/information-technology/cybersecurity-stocks/) platform comprising 34 modules that address several large security markets. The company is best known for its dominance in endpoint security, which protects devices such as servers, workstations, and mobile devices. But it also has a strong presence in identity protection, cloud security, threat intelligence, and managed detection and response.
CrowdStrike differentiates itself by delivering dozens of cybersecurity products through one platform powered by a lightweight sensor that can be installed without system restarts. It streams telemetry data back to its AI engine, continuously improving its threat-detection capabilities. CrowdStrike claims "industry-leading efficacy and low false positives."
CrowdStrike reported encouraging financial results in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended in July 2026. Revenue increased 26% to $1.4 billion, and non-GAAP earnings increased 35% to $0.31 per diluted share. CEO George Kurtz called it the "best quarter in CrowdStrike's history."
CrowdStrike is well-positioned to maintain its momentum as cyberattacks become more sophisticated with the help of AI. Wall Street expects the company's adjusted earnings to grow at 28% annually through the fiscal year ending in January 2028. Even so, the current valuation of 230 times earnings looks absurdly expensive.
Indeed, among 57 Wall Street analysts, CrowdStrike has a median target price of $245 per share. That implies 4% downside from its current share price of $255. CrowdStrike has a strong position in a growing industry, but the stock is too expensive after its 115% year-to-date gain. Investors should keep this name on their watchlists for now.

# Opening date confirmed for Ashford’s first Taco Bell at Waterbrook Park, Sevington
![Google](/_assets/googlelight.png) ![](/_assets/twitterxarticle_2.jpg) ![Public Notices Portal](/_assets/pnp_logo.png)
Check the latest public notices in your area - planning, roads and licensing
Kent’s newest Taco Bell is ready to open – two years after planning permission was approved.
The branch is one of the latest arrivals at Ashford’s Waterbrook Park in Sevington.
![Ashford’s first Taco Bell is set to open. Picture: iStock](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 1156 800'%3E%3C/svg%3E) ![Ashford’s first Taco Bell is set to open. Picture: iStock](/_media/img/18K0RQ4OUKD18LZKXFUH.jpg)
Construction began on the restaurant, which serves Mexican fast food, in March.
It was supposed to welcome its first customers in the summer, but the American giant said delays in supplier timelines pushed this back.
Now, bosses have confirmed it will open at 11am on Tuesday (September 29).
Taco Bell marketing director Lucy Dee said: “We’re excited to open our doors and connect with the people of Ashford.
“At Taco Bell, we’re known around the world for pushing boundaries with bold flavours, category-defining innovation and unforgettable brand experiences.”
The first 100 customers will be given a Taco Bell T-shirt, while one guest will win free food for a year.
It comes after [KFC opened a branch at Waterbrook Park in August](https://www.kentonline.co.uk/ashford/news/kfc-opens-town-s-third-restaurant-344365/).
The site is also set to see the arrival of a new David Lloyd health club on land opposite Aldi, filling a spot previously earmarked for an Amazon warehouse.
The facility, which will create 100 jobs, is due to feature three tennis courts and four swimming pools.
But KentOnline has already revealed the health club is not expected to open until at least 2027 due to a planning dispute involving landowner GSE, ABC, and Kent County Council.
![Taco Bell is just one of several brands coming to Ashford's Waterbrook Park](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 1509 1001'%3E%3C/svg%3E) ![Taco Bell is just one of several brands coming to Ashford's Waterbrook Park](/_media/img/JEZRPFJFIH8VDR3R456A.jpg) ![KFC opened in Ashford's Waterbrook Park in August](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 5466 3901'%3E%3C/svg%3E) ![KFC opened in Ashford's Waterbrook Park in August](/_media/img/1QOVL5O4NU2T9FOSIH84.jpg)
Meanwhile, Aldi opened its second Ashford supermarket on Waterbrook Park in October.
With more than 7,500 restaurants worldwide, Taco Bell’s opening in Ashford marks the next phase of its continued expansion, particularly across Europe.
The chain has more than 150 locations in England, including in Canterbury, Ashford, Chatham, Maidstone, Broadstairs and Dover.
